title: 1925 Sonny Clay and 1926 Reb Spikes records
summary: Redd lists personnel and tunes for the Sonny Clay Plantation Orchestra record and the Reb Spikes sides including Sheffield's Blues.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: MS. REDD: 1925, Andrew Blakeney recorded with the Sonny Clay's Plantation Orchestra in Los Angeles, on Vocalian Label, 1000. This was a 78 disc. The personnel included Ernest Coycault, first trumpet; W.B. Woodman, trombone; Leonard Davidson, clarinet; and James Carson, clarinet and tenor sax; Louis Dodd, alto sax, banjo, guitar; Willie McDaniel, drums.
Mr. Blakeney states that he did not recall the presence of a Mr. Fitzgerald on this particular date. The sounds recorded were "Plantation Blues" and "Chicago Breakdown."

This was the very first recording that Mr. Blakeney made upon his arrival in Los Angeles. He states that he had been here approximately two months and was very happy to do this date with Sonny Clay's Plantation Orchestra, 1925.

1926. Mr. Blakeney recorded with the Reb Spikes Legion Club 45's, in Hollywood. Included in the orchestra at this time were Blakeney and Russell Massengail (spelling), trumpet; Leon White, trombone; Les Hite, clarinet, alto sax and vocals; William Calhoun, clarinet, tenor sax and vocal; Spikes, bass sax; Gene White, piano; Lionel Hampton, drums.
Lionel Hampton also did a "spoken vocal" on this record date. It appears that the musicians were making shouts on the record, rather than singing a particular melody.

Recorded were the songs, 'My Mamie's Blues,' and 'Sheffield's Blues.' "Sheffield's Blues" became somewhat of a hit for the group as it was written for a legendary detective in the area, one of the few black detectives at this time.
Mr. Sheffield was known for breaking down doors to bootlegging joints
and even a private residence if he thought that booze was being sold.
